segments.t: This is The Kitchen, a comedy set in the kitchen of Claude Monet, a smart restaurant in Moscow. In this episode, Max and Vika are keeping their romance secret, and the head chef picks a fight with the chef next door over a parking space. We start at the bar, where Nastya has a quiet proposal for Kostya. First the whole thing in the local language, and don't worry if you miss words.
А я хочу остаться у тебя сегодня.
Нет, нам пора сделать следующий шаг.
Мы просто проведём этот вечер вместе.
И мы никому ничего не скажем?
Now the slow version, with Nastya doing most of the talking.
'Kostya, what are you doing right now?' The language says 'what you now do', with the little
for 'you' tucked in the middle. There's one word for 'do' and it covers 'are doing' as well, because there is no need for a separate 'are ...ing'.
'I am standing and polishing glasses.' Same thing here. 'I stand and polish' means 'I am standing and polishing'. Notice he uses for polishing,
, grows from 'rub', which is exactly what you do to a glass.
А я хочу остаться у тебя сегодня.
'And I want to stay at your place today.' 'At your place' is
, which means 'at you'. The locals use it for anyone's home.
'At my place? Did someone kick you out?' He answers with the same idea, now as a question. 'Someone kicked you out' puts 'you' first,
, and the little ending on the word for 'who' turns it into 'someone'.
Нет, нам пора сделать следующий шаг.
'No, it is time for us to take the next step.' Word for word, 'to us time', which gives 'it is time for us'. Notice for 'next',
, comes from a word meaning 'to follow'.
'Do you want to get married?' Careful with this one:
means 'to go out behind a husband', and only a woman can do it. A man would use a different word, so this is a question you can only put to a woman.
'Kostik, you are so funny!' 'Kostik' is a pet name made from Kostya with a small-making ending, the way English adds 'ie' to a name. The term for 'funny' is
Мы просто проведём этот вечер вместе.
'We will simply spend this evening together.' Spending time takes its own verb,
, and it is never used for money. Notice for together,
, is an early word that you can reuse everywhere.
И мы никому ничего не скажем?
'And we will not tell anyone anything?' Three negatives pile up:
. That is how the language makes it emphatic, and it isn't a mistake. Word for word, 'to no one nothing we won't say'.
'This will be our little secret.' Here
means 'will be' and is spoken out loud, and the term for 'little',
, makes the secret sound cosy. The term for 'our',
, has no ending added because the term for secret is masculine.
'Great, that sounds very logical.' The word
means 'it sounds', from the same root as the term for a sound. The word for logical,
, ends in an 'o', showing it is the 'how' form.
'I will quickly buy beautiful candles.' We can break down the sentence:
means 'I will buy', and there's no helper word in it. Notice for candles,
, is a plural, and the term for beautiful has a plural ending to match.
'Good, make this evening magical!' Nastya gives an order, then names what the evening should turn into. The term for magical,
, comes from the term for wizard, with the ending of 'made into'. And now all of it again, without the commentary.
А я хочу остаться у тебя сегодня.
Нет, нам пора сделать следующий шаг.
Мы просто проведём этот вечер вместе.
И мы никому ничего не скажем?
Kostya runs off to buy candles, which tells you he understood exactly what she meant. Let's see how long the secret lasts. Until next time.
